correctness.rationale: With axes separated by 0<θ≤π/2, each Bθ pulse changes the Bloch colatitude of the first-axis north pole by ≤2θ; induction using opposite-meridian half-turns and azimuthal freedom gives exact reachable cap {U:β(U)≤min(2mθ,π)} including m=0 and poles. The free final A rotation spans the Hopf fiber of each reachable Bloch ray. SU(2) trace identity reduces optimal phase-insensitive process fidelity to squared ray overlap, cos²(d/2), and nearest cap projection gives cos²(((β−c)_+)/2) globally. Uniform Haar SU(2) projects to uniform Bloch sphere, with β-density sinβ/2; integrating yields the stated atom, survival law and exact mean error (1+cos c)/4−(π−c)sin c/8. Taylor expansion at c=π gives δ^4/96−δ^6/1440+O(δ^8), while worst error sin²(δ/2)∼δ²/4. Independent numerical Haar integrals at c=0,.8,1.4,π and independent symbolic Taylor calculation corroborate; finite checks do not prove all-target cap equality.

originality.rationale: Hamada 2014 proves stronger pointwise exact-synthesis minimal rotation counts and constructive cap geometry: this is explicitly prior and not claimed. Garbaravičius–Wolf 2026 studies number of switches for arbitrary unitaries at fixed axes and expectation over random basis pairs, not fixed-budget approximation fidelity distribution over Haar targets. The new assessed claim is optimal process-fidelity *beyond* exact reachable set and its Haar-target law, including quartic mean versus quadratic worst-case. No equivalence found in inspected sources; direct metric projection/Haar-integration derivability and an unread 2026 full text remain priority risks.
